To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CDC31 product of the yeast Saccharomyces is a component of a substructure of the spindle pole bodies (SPBs) called the half bridge, that CDC31 protein binds calcium, that CDC31 is an essential protein, and that CDC31 defines a family of calcium- binding, centrosome-associated proteins.
CDC31 is essential for cell division, that CDC31 is an SPB component, that the SPB is a calcium binding protein, and that the SPB has a previously unreported substructure.
CDC31 is essential for yeast cell viability, is a Ca2+ binding protein and is a component of SPB half bridge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a novel protein component of the SPBs and with the determination of its localization and function.
the structure and function of the SPB and the mechanism of spindle pole duplication.
the structure and function of the SPB and with the role of CDC31 as a component of the structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CDC31 is an SPB-associated protein which binds Ca2+ in a specific fashion.
the CDC31 protein is a component of an SPB substructure that is essential for SPB function.
the SPB is a highly conserved organelle that plays a critical role in the control of cell division.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CDC31 is an integral component of the SPBs of Saccharomyce s cerevisiae.
CDC31 protein is a Ca2+-binding protein that is localized to the SPB and that it is a component of a structure called the half bridge.
the SPBs of S. cerevisiae have a structure similar to that of the centrosomes of higher cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SPB is a complex structure, and the identification of new SPB components will help us understand how SPB structure and dynamics relate to cell cycle control.
we have identified a new component of the SPBs of yeast and that this protein binds calcium.
the SPB half bridge, which we show here is the site of CDC31, is an integral part of the SPB and is required for cell division.
